title: prompt-drafts-and-prompt-library-experiments-jordan
content:
Notes / scratchpad for prompt library experiments - Jordan (personal)

Purpose:
- Collect a set of prompt templates and few-shot examples that we can iterate on for Redwood customer-facing prompt library.
- Record failure cases and quick mitigation strategies to add to the docs.
- Keep a running log of quick experiments (model, prompt variant, high-level result).

High-level goals:
- Few-shot templates that bias for concise, factual responses (for assistant-style generation and summarization tasks).
- Templates for instruction-to-API conversions (i.e., map free text requests into structured function calls / JSON).
- Safety mitigations for hallucination when answering about product/SLAs.

Current prompt templates (working drafts):

1) Concise factual assistant (use for internal Q&A and product knowledge)

Prompt-template A (concise-fact):
Instruction: You are a concise, factual assistant. Answer in 2-4 sentences. If the answer is unknown, say "I don't know" and suggest where to check (docs or ticket).
Context: {context: up to 500 tokens of product notes / doc excerpts}
User: {question}
Response format: plain text, 2-4 sentences, one bullet with a source link if available.

Few-shot (inline examples):
Example 1
Context: Redwood Dedicated offers dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput.
User: How does Dedicated differ from Hosted API?
Assistant: Dedicated provides reserved GPU capacity, isolation, and SLA-backed latency/uptime. Hosted API is multi-tenant, easier to start, and usage-billed.

Example 2
Context: Private deployments support VPC and on-prem installs with KMS/HSM for key management.
User: Does Private support customer-managed keys?
Assistant: Yes — Private supports KMS/HSM integrations for customer-managed keys; see the security guide for setup steps.

Notes: this template reduces verbosity and forces an explicit "I don't know" fallback.

2) Structured output / function call template (for mapping to API)

Prompt-template B (json-output):
Instruction: Read the user request and produce a JSON object with keys: intent, entities (list), confidence (0-1). If unsure, set confidence < 0.5 and put best-effort values. Do NOT include extra commentary.
User: {user_text}

Few-shot examples:
Input: "Create a new inference deployment for the analytics team, gpu type A100, region us-west-2, scale 4"
Output (json): {"intent":"create_deployment","entities":[{"type":"team","value":"analytics"},{"type":"gpu","value":"A100"},{"type":"region","value":"us-west-2"},{"type":"scale","value":"4"}],"confidence":0.93}

Input: "Need a cheaper option for batch embedding runs"
Output (json): {"intent":"optimize_cost","entities":[{"type":"workload","value":"batch-embeddings"}],"confidence":0.55}

Notes: must validate that assistant outputs valid JSON only. Add a regex-based post-check in client: if parse fails, re-prompt with: "Reply only with valid JSON matching the schema".

3) Safety / Hallucination mitigation template

Prompt-template C (source-first):
Instruction: When answering product questions, prefer to cite a source. Prepend answers with '[source-id]' when quoting exact docs. If you cannot find a source in the provided context, respond: "I don't have a source for that—please check internal docs or ask the product team." Keep tone neutral.

Failure cases observed and quick notes:
- Failure: Model hallucinates release dates for features not yet shipped.
  Mitigation: Add explicit instruction: "Do not invent dates; if unknown, say unknown." Also strip system prompt that encourages creativity for product Q&A.
- Failure: JSON outputs include extra commentary after JSON ("Here is the object: {...}").
  Mitigation: client-side strict-parse check + re-prompt template to enforce pure JSON; also use stop sequences.
- Failure: Model ignores few-shot examples when context is long.
  Mitigation: move crucial examples to the start of context and use instruction to "follow the examples strictly"; reduce number of examples.

Experiment log (quick):
- 2026-01-12 | model: gpt-4o-mini | prompt A vs A+source-first
  Result: A produced verbose answers ~3-6 sentences. A+source-first reduced to 2-3 sentences and increased exact-source citations in 62% of runs. Notes: still hallucinated when context lacked explicit doc.
- 2026-01-19 | model: open-llm-2.1 | prompt B (json-output)
  Result: 81% valid JSON; 19% had trailing commentary. Client-side parse + re-prompt recovered 14/19 of the failures.
- 2026-02-05 | model: redwood-internal-qa-1 | prompt C
  Result: Good at refusing to answer out-of-context questions (refused 94% of out-of-scope prompts). Tends to be too terse.

Evaluation checklist (for moving a prompt into the library):
- Reproducibility: same prompt + seed/temperature produces stable outputs (manual check across 10 runs)
- Safety: no hallucinations on a held-out set of 40 queries about product SLAs and features
- Parseability: structured outputs parse without transformation in >= 95% runs
- Latency: prompt length increases token cost—prefer examples that are concise

TODO / next steps:
- [ ] Consolidate 10 best templates into a single "prompt-library-v1" doc and add to Confluence (confluence:PROD-PROMPT-LIB-42)
- [ ] Add automated test harness for json-output prompts (Jira: MLINF-317)
- [ ] Get Prod team review on safety wording re: SLAs
- [ ] Move source-first template into internal answers bot for docs search flow

Quick notes to self / heuristics:
- Always include an explicit fallback phrase ("I don't know" style) for any factual product Q&A.
- For few-shot examples use highly representative edge cases (billing, security, private deployment) rather than many similar examples.
- If model tends to be verbose, add hard limits in prompt: "Respond in N sentences" or use "TL;DR: <one-sentence>" pattern.

Scratch examples to try next run (copy-paste):
---
System: You are Redwood's product assistant. Do not invent facts. If unknown, say "Unknown — check internal docs".
User: "What's the SLA for Redwood Dedicated?"
Context: (attach docs excerpt: dedicated-sla.md)

Expected: "Redwood Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime for production nodes. See dedicated-sla.md for details."
---

Edge-case prompt (billing ambiguity):
User: "How much will my monthly bill be if I run 100M tokens on hosted?"
Instruction: Ask a clarifying question if rate/plan unknown: "Which plan are you on (trial/standard/enterprise)?"

Links / useful references:
- Confluence: PROD-PROMPT-LIB-42 (master doc)
- Jira: MLINF-317 (json-output test harness)
- Slack thread: #prompt-library (search: "json output failures")
- GitHub: repo/example-prompts (branch: experiments/jordan/prompt-cleanup)

Notes for future formatting in library:
- Keep template names short and kebab-case (e.g., concise-fact, json-output, source-first)
- Include a short "when to use" and "failure modes" section per template
- Track owner + last-validated date on each template (metadata)

End of scratchpad.
